data: The Client reported a rough week, noting a panic attack on Tuesday at the grocery store checkout line with a pounding heart, which led to leaving the cart and walking out. The Client reported thoughts of passing out in front of everyone and being judged as crazy, rating the belief at 90% in the moment and 40% later at home. The Client completed two thought records out of the assigned three, covering the grocery store incident and a work event. Sleep was reported as poor, averaging about four hours a night with waking around 3:00 AM. The Client reported starting sertraline 50 mg approximately two weeks ago per their primary care doctor, with initial mild nausea that has since resolved. The Client denied any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation, stating they just want the panic to stop. The Client mentioned feeling unsupported by their sister Dana, who tells them to "just push through it," though the Client declined inviting Dana to a session at this time.

The Client participated in a 50-minute individual CBT session. The Therapist conducted interoceptive exposure in-session by having the Client spin in a chair for 30 seconds. The Client rated their anxiety as a 6 out of 10 immediately following the spinning exercise, which decreased to a 3 out of 10 within two minutes. No formal standardized measure scores besides subjective anxiety ratings were assessed this session.

The Client demonstrates partial progress toward treatment goals, having completed two thought records out of the three assigned. The Client recognized a cognitive shift when evaluating a past panic attack belief of passing out at 90% down to 40% later at home. The Client engaged in in-session interoceptive exposure (spinning in the chair for 30 seconds), reporting that anxiety peaked at a 6 and decreased to a 3 within two minutes, recognizing that physiological sensations peak and pass.

Current diagnosis remains F41.0 Panic disorder. Risk level for self-harm or suicide is assessed as none, as the Client explicitly denied any thoughts of hurting themselves or of not wanting to be alive. Response to CBT treatment is positive, with active participation in cognitive restructuring and exposure tasks.
